planning_note: Organize into declaration, combinational decode, clocked registers/FSM, and output port binding. All WISHBONE-visible outputs are registered per spec. Multi‑cycle BD write handled by a dedicated FSM.
module_frame:
module sd_controller_wb (
    // WISHBONE slave interface
    input  wire             wb_clk_i,
    input  wire             wb_rst_i,
    input  wire [31:0]      wb_dat_i,
    output reg  [31:0]      wb_dat_o,
    input  wire [7:0]       wb_adr_i,
    input  wire [3:0]       wb_sel_i,
    input  wire             wb_we_i,
    input  wire             wb_cyc_i,
    input  wire             wb_stb_i,
    output reg              wb_ack_o,

    // Control outputs to other sub‑modules
    output reg              we_m_tx_bd,
    output reg              we_m_rx_bd,
    output reg              new_cmd,
    output reg              we_ack,
    output reg              int_ack,
    output reg              cmd_int_busy,
    output reg              int_busy,
    output reg              Bd_isr_reset,
    output reg              normal_isr_reset,
    output reg              error_isr_reset,

    // Data master interface
    input  wire             write_req_s,
    input  wire [15:0]      cmd_set_s,
    input  wire [31:0]      cmd_arg_s,

    // Configuration registers exposed as outputs
    output reg  [31:0]      argument_reg,
    output reg  [15:0]      cmd_setting_reg,
    output reg  [7:0]       software_reset_reg,
    output reg  [15:0]      time_out_reg,
    output reg  [15:0]      normal_int_signal_enable_reg,
    output reg  [15:0]      error_int_signal_enable_reg,
    output reg  [7:0]       clock_divider,
    output reg  [7:0]       Bd_isr_enable_reg,

    // Status/response inputs from rest of design
    input  wire [15:0]      status_reg,
    input  wire [31:0]      cmd_resp_1,
    input  wire [16:0]      normal_int_status_reg,
    input  wire [16:0]      error_int_status_reg,
    input  wire [16:0]      Bd_Status_reg,
    input  wire [7:0]       Bd_isr_reg,

    // BD data outputs to buffer descriptor blocks
    output reg  [RAM_MEM_WIDTH-1:0] dat_in_m_tx_bd,
    output reg  [RAM_MEM_WIDTH-1:0] dat_in_m_rx_bd
);

// <block: decl_core>

// <block: port_assign>

endmodule

structural_blocks.purpose: Declare all internal storage (register file for configuration registers, BD write FSM state, output register signals), internal wires for combinational logic, and constants.
must_appear: register storage for all addressable registers: argument, cmd_setting, software_reset, timeout, normal_int_enable, error_int_enable, clock_divider, Bd_isr_enable
output registers for ports listed as outputs (argument_reg, etc. may be directly exposed from internal regfile)
BD FSM state (e.g., idle, waiting 1st word, waiting 2nd word)
may_appear: constant definitions for register addresses and widths

structural_blocks.purpose: Combinational logic that decodes wb_adr_i for read mux, write enable target, BD write condition, reset‑pulse generation, and next‑state logic for the BD FSM; derives data sources for reads.
must_appear: address decoder and read mux that covers all documented register addresses
write enable signals for each register
conditions for BD write multi‑cycle (depends on RAM_MEM_WIDTH)
generation of registered output values for output ports (driven from next‑state logic, e.g., wb_ack_o_next)

structural_blocks.purpose: All clocked processes: update internal register file, BD FSM state, all registered output ports (wb_ack_o, wb_dat_o, we_m_tx_bd, we_m_rx_bd, new_cmd, we_ack, int_ack, cmd_int_busy, int_busy, Bd_isr_reset, normal_isr_reset, error_isr_reset, and BD data ports). Reset sets default values per spec.
structural_blocks.code_shape: sequential always @(posedge wb_clk_i or posedge wb_rst_i) cluster
must_appear: reset behavior exactly as spec: int_ack → 1, other variables → 0, configuration registers → documented default values
register write logic for all writable registers
BD multi‑cycle write handling (16‑bit RAM width case requires two writes)
registered output port updates aligned with combinational next‑state signals
may_appear: separate always blocks for BD FSM and general register/write logic if cleaner

structural_blocks.purpose: Direct assignments of internal register/stored values to module output ports. For outputs that are already registered in B3, this block may be trivial; for argument_reg, time_out_reg etc., it connects the internal storage to the output port (no extra logic).
must_appear: direct connections for all configuration register outputs (argument_reg, cmd_setting_reg, software_reset_reg, time_out_reg, …)
BD data output ports from internal BD data registers

semantic_modes.meaning: simple Wishbone read/write to configuration registers
multi‑cycle write to BD RX or BD TX with int_ack handshake

state_model.notes: controls we_m_xx_bd, int_ack timing, and BD data capture

global_invariants: wb_ack_o is registered and only asserted in response to wb_cyc_i & wb_stb_i when int_ack is high
all outputs driven to the rest of sdc_controller are registered on wb_clk_i rising edge
open_semantic_questions: exact read data latency (1 cycle from address valid to wb_dat_o update) implied by registered output
BD write timing when RAM_MEM_WIDTH is 32 versus 16 – spec gives high‑level process

responsibilities: provide all storage that will be written/read by other blocks
timing_semantics: values are updated in B3 on rising edge
coupling_rules: B2 and B3 reference these declared objects
forbidden_drift: do not add extra state not implied by the spec

responsibilities: generate write strobes and BD control conditions
produce next‑state signals for all registered outputs and BD FSM
timing_semantics: purely combinational; must complete within one clock period
forbidden_drift: do not create asynchronous paths from inputs to outputs; outputs depend only on registered values from B3 and combinational logic

responsibilities: execute all state updates: register file writes, BD FSM transitions, output port registration
enforce reset values as per spec
timing_semantics: all updates occur at posedge wb_clk_i (or asynchronously reset when wb_rst_i asserted)
wb_ack_o is registered, meeting Wishbone B.3 requirements
touched_objects: all configuration registers, BD FSM state, all output port registers
coupling_rules: drives internal values that B4 combines to ports
forbidden_drift: do not invent combinational paths from output registers to external ports except through B4

responsibilities: map internal signals to module ports, handling any trivial width conversions
timing_semantics: entirely combinatorial; must not introduce additional pipeline stages
forbidden_drift: do not add extra mux or gating

chosen_decisions.decision: Decompose into declaration, combinational decode, clocked update, and port binding blocks.
chosen_decisions.reason: Aligns with typical Wishbone register file designs and isolates BD write FSM handling.

deferred_decisions: Exact state encoding and transition conditions for BD FSM (will depend on final RAM_MEM_WIDTH logic)
How read path reacts to BD registers: they are write‑only; read may return 0 or undefined – spec unclear; may default to 0.
Whether normal_isr_reset / error_isr_reset / Bd_isr_reset are pulsed for one cycle or remain asserted while write is active; spec says “writing any value resets”, implying a pulse.
structural_risks: Large combinational decode block (B2) could become complex; might later need splitting into sub‑decode and data mux blocks if synthesis tools struggle.
Register file declaration (B1) may need explicit width‑parameterized arrays if many registers share similar coding patterns.
behavioral_risks: The exact timing relationship between write_req_s and we_ack is not fully captured; may require clarification during local generation.

The module outputs some registers directly (e.g., argument_reg) that are also part of the internal register file; if the spec expects these outputs to be updated immediately on write (same cycle), registered outputs satisfy that if output registers are directly connected to internal storage (the spec’s own statement that outputs are registered means a one‑cycle delay, which may be acceptable).
